messages:
alex: FYI spotted a regression in production attention p99 after yesterday's batching heuristic change. nsys capture uploaded: https://infralogs/redwood/nsys/3141592653 (internal). Looking at the kernel timeline there's a recurring 'kv_write_back' serialization every ~120ms that lines up with tail latency spikes. Anyone else seeing a KV write stall pattern?

mina: I repro'd locally and saw the same alignment. nvprof/nsys sampling shows long gaps where launches wait on a write fence. Culprit seems to be a kernel that takes an exclusive lock before writing KV shards. Repro steps: run the mixed seq harness with seqs [512, 64] -- reproduces in ~20s.

mina: Example capture command I used:

```
nsys profile -o /tmp/attn_kv_regress --trace=cuda,cuda_driver,osrt \
  python -m tests.attn_repro --seqs 512,64 --batch 8 --iters 200
```

raj: digging into the selector logs, the new batching heuristic moved the packing threshold so mixed-length packs now prefer 'attn_fallback_v3'. That kernel holds an internal write_mutex during KV write batches, which serializes following requests. Older path 'attn_streamed_v1' did async writebacks and avoided the mutex.

raj: quick experiment: force selector to legacy pack and the writequeue stalls disappear. Env overrides I tested: `REDWOOD_BATCH_TILE_THRESHOLD=0.2` or `KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy_pack`. Not a long-term fix but useful for a canary. (reaction :eyes:)

perf-bot: Automated trace analysis ready: https://infralogs/redwood/nsys/3141592700 — highlights: recurring kv_write_back peaks ~4.8MB/s bursts, mean write latency 1.8ms, but serialized gaps coincide with attn_forward kernels >60ms.

sophia: I ran the override + microbench. p99 drops from ~240ms -> ~180ms in our harness, throughput down ~5%. Side note: 'attn_opt_flash_v2' shows register_pressure spikes on A100-simulated runs, which increases kernel time and creates a backlog of pending KV writes. Could be two orthogonal problems colliding.

sophia: Short-term proposal: 1) rollout per-model KERNEL_SELECTOR override as hotfix; 2) recompile attn_opt_flash with reduced register allocation flag to test impact (e.g. --reduce-registers); 3) add perfetto markers around KV enqueue/dequeue to correlate writequeue depth with kernel launches.

mina: +1 on markers. I can add trace points in KV write path: `tracepoint(inference, kv_enqueue, size, seq_id)` and `tracepoint(inference, kv_dequeue, size, seq_id)`. That will let perfetto show queue depth over time.

alex: Great plan. Can someone spin a canary with KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy_pack + reduced-register build for the attn image? I'll schedule a 30m triage in #eng-runtime at 12:30 PT to review the canary traces. Thanks all :thumbsup:

alex: Also adding checklist for triage: reproduce with harness, attach nsys and perfetto links, include kernel selection logs (selector.debug=1), and the env used for the canary.
